title: Section 12 Limitation Act — Time for copies

content.overview: Exclude the starting day. For appeal, revision and review, also exclude the time requisitely spent obtaining the copy.
content.study: Requisite means the time the copying office actually needed after a proper application. Dilatory applicants do not get the calendar they wasted.

learningObjectives: Apply the provision to a limitation calculation or factual problem.
Distinguish the provision from related limitation rules.
enhancement.definition: Section 12 excludes specified periods when computing limitation, including the day from which the prescribed period is reckoned and, in specified appeals, revisions and reviews, requisite time for obtaining the copy of the relevant decree or order.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Limitation is computed after applying the statutory exclusions in Section 12; the provision is a computation rule, not a general condonation provision.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Limitation Act, 1963, Section 12 and its subsections concerning suits, appeals, revisions, reviews and copies.
essentialIngredients: Identify the proceeding and subsection of Section 12 that applies.
For specified appellate/revisional/review proceedings, identify the requisite copying period.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 12 adjusts the arithmetic of limitation. The Supreme Court has applied Section 12(1) to exclude the day from which limitation is reckoned and has recognized its role in calculating limitation periods in special statutory proceedings unless excluded by the governing law.
examples: If a limitation period begins from the date of a judgment or order, the day of that judgment/order is excluded under Section 12(1). Where the provision applicable to an appeal permits exclusion of requisite time for obtaining a copy, that copying period is also removed from the computation.
enhancement.distinctions: Section 12 excludes specified time from computation; Section 14 excludes time spent bona fide prosecuting the same matter in a court unable to entertain it; Section 5 concerns condonation of eligible delay.

caseLaw.name: My Preferred Transformation & Hospitality Pvt. Ltd. v. M/s Faridabad Implements Pvt. Ltd.
caseLaw.holding: The Supreme Court discussed Section 12 and reiterated that the day from which a limitation period is to be reckoned is excluded in computation.
